checks: Source 0590f45b97fc9c04:03, Theorem (1) and §§1–4, states the same two-measure constant and uniform-body consequence. The frozen proof handles r=2 by the median and gives the explicit projective degree argument.

After an orthogonal change of coordinates, integrate the log-concave density over the one-dimensional orthogonal complement of the projection space. Prékopa's Theorems 6 and 8 give log-concavity. A ball in the positive set projects onto a ball of positive marginal density. This does not require compact original support.

The strict target alpha produces full relative interior in each depth region using uniform cap continuity on the compact projected unit sphere. The outward direction of any nonzero candidate puts its through-cap in the tail outside its radius, giving boundedness uniformly in u.

Under moving hyperplanes the rotated normals give outer semicontinuity. An interior feasible point is strictly feasible because equality in a proper direction would lose positive slab mass under a small allowed move; the marginal's interior positive continuous representative supplies that slab. Its strict gap survives small rotations by compactness of unit normals. Approximation along an interior segment and minimum-norm optimality therefore identify every subsequential limit.

The difference field is continuous, even and perpendicular to u. If nonzero, its normalization is homotopic to the identity by the displayed quarter-circle path. In even sphere dimension the antipodal map has degree -1, and in odd sphere dimension the projective quotient is orientable and the double cover has degree two. Both contradict degree one for an even map.

The line condition tests only perpendicular normals. For alpha_j approaching gamma, the positive initial alpha uniformly bounds offsets. Rotating any limit normal by orthogonal projection and using the nullity of its limiting hyperplane passes the lower bound at the limiting line for both measures. For compact convex uniform supports, strict separation from the projection would give a zero-mass cap, so the line meets each body.

dependencies.hypotheses: In dimension s=r−1≥2 the positive marginal density has mass one, full-dimensional convex positive interior and extended convex inverse power, since exp((−log f)/beta) is convex for beta>r=s+1. Use its attained lower bound gamma_s with its boundary representative. At s=1 the proof uses an absolutely continuous median instead.
Theorems 6 and 8 give that integration over the remaining coordinate after an orthogonal change preserves log-concavity of a multivariate probability density.
dependencies.reference: Prékopa, On logarithmic concave measures and functions, Theorems 6 and 8

overlap.comparison: Gives the ordinary one-measure projected bound, but no simultaneous common line or continuous strict-depth selection across the moving normal spaces.
An arbitrary finite Borel measure has a single ambient point at its Helly centerpoint threshold. It does not give a line at this common sharp log-concave projection threshold for two measures.

readability: The proof keeps the strict-level selection separate from the limiting exact threshold. The exact constant is per measure for halfspaces containing the whole line.

summary: Two full-dimensional log-concave probabilities admit one line that has the sharp ordinary projected depth constant in both orthogonal marginals.
